text.young: Munch, munch! Your teeth chop the food and spit makes it soft and slippery.
text.junior: Teeth break the food into small pieces, and saliva starts digesting starch. The tongue rolls it into a soft ball called a bolus.

text.young: Gulp! The food slides down your food pipe as its muscles squeeze it along.
text.junior: After you swallow, waves of muscle called peristalsis push the bolus down the oesophagus in a few seconds.

text.young: Splash! Your stomach churns the food with strong juices, like a washing machine.
text.junior: The stomach churns the food with acid and enzymes for a few hours, turning it into a thick liquid called chyme.

text.young: Wiggle! In your long small intestine, the goodness from the food soaks into your blood.
text.junior: Bile from the liver and juices from the pancreas finish digestion, and tiny villi absorb nutrients into the blood.

text.young: Nearly done! Your large intestine soaks up water, and the leftovers become poo.
text.junior: The large intestine absorbs water and salts. What is left is stored as waste until it leaves the body.
